merger_description:
Apiam Animal Health Pty Ltd (**Apiam**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital in Caroline Springs Veterinary Centre & Animal Hospital Pty Ltd (**CS Veterinary Centre**) (**the Acquisition**). CS Veterinary Centre owns and operates the business known as Caroline Springs Veterinary Centre and Animal Hospital.

Apiam is a rural veterinary businesses, comprising more than 80 veterinary clinics and ancillary business sites across Australia, and supplies a range of veterinary services across Australia, including companion animal, equine, dairy, beef cattle, sheep and goat, pig, poultry and mixed animal veterinary services, together with veterinary diagnostics, emergency and after-hours services, reproductive and herd health services, and pathology, laboratory and advisory services. Apiam is ultimately owned and controlled by funds managed and advised by Adamantem Capital Management.

CS Veterinary Centre is a full-service companion animal veterinary practice located in Caroline Springs, Victoria. The practice provides general veterinary care, pathology services and surgical procedures.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Apiam and CS
Veterinary Centre in the supply of veterinary services in the
Caroline Springs area, and
b. there are alternative suppliers of veterinary services in the
Caroline Springs area and more broadly at the regional, state
and national levels.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
